name: kalide-owned-scaffold
body: Kalide-owned scaffold: the content kalide itself writes into a project and still owns — the two embedded author-guide pairs (each a full `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` guide, domain.value.agent-guide / domain.value.library-agent-guide, plus its short `AGENTS.md` pointer, agent-guide-reference) and the minimal `kalide init` seed tree (the seed `templates/library.yaml`, the `hello` slide template with its `example.md`, the default theme and the starter slide `slides/1-hello.md`; cli-init-minimal-seed). It is the only content upgrade may refresh; every other project file is author content and is never written. It is scoped per project kind and scaffold form rather than applied globally: a no-arg seed deck owns the whole seed tree; an external-library deck (`templates:` configured) owns only its deck-root guide pair and never a local `templates/` or starter slide; a library owns its library-root guide pair and its seeded default theme, never templates or media. `kalide.yaml` is the deck config the author edits and is not whole-file scaffold — its structure is migration territory. A member is rewritten only when it is present and byte-identical to a known released version of that same file; the full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` is the one exception and is also written when absent, while the `AGENTS.md` pointer is brought to the reference scheme (created when absent, migrated from a known released full guide, appended to with the reference line when it is author content without the string, or left untouched when it already carries the string — the one permitted modification of an author-owned `AGENTS.md`, global.constraint.upgrade-never-clobbers); a deleted seed starter file is never re-created; and a present file matching no known released version is author content, left untouched and reported. It is a descriptor of the upgrade domain, realising through its containing domain.group.upgrade rather than carrying its own `realised-by` edge.
